text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Frederick Chiluba called for an end to vandalism of public property, saying this was necessary for efforts to rehabilitate the country's rundown infrastructure to succeed.
- The government warned opposition leaders they would be to blame if there were disruptions of peace in the country.
- The goverment has terminated the contract of the state-run Zambia Daily Mail's editor, Patrick Fungamwango.

- The international watchdog group Human Rights Watch/Africa has called on the government to replace commissioners to a newly constituted human rights commission and to appoint others in a more transparent fashion.

- Amnesty International is to ask donors at a Consultative Group meeting which opens in Paris on Thursday to seek the Zambian government's assurance that it will improve its human rights record before making aid pledges.
